advice: The GLA has no aircraft whatsoever. Any air investment you make is unanswerable except by Quad Cannons and Stinger Sites — scout for those, then fly.
Destroyed GLA buildings leave holes that rebuild cheaply. Killing a structure is a delay, not a removal: kill the workers too.
Watch for Tunnel Networks near your base. A tunnel is a teleport pad for an army you never saw cross the map.
USA units cost more than yours. Trading evenly is winning — force engagements you can afford to lose.
Airfields are large and fragile. A raid that kills parked aircraft costs them far more than it costs you.
They are weakest before the first Airfield lands. Apply pressure early or accept a late-game air war.
Do not let five identical Chinese units sit together — the horde bonus makes that ball much stronger than its cost.
China has almost no stealth and poor detection. A stealthed or flanking force will get behind them.
Their units are slow. Kiting, artillery and air all beat the Chinese ground ball if you refuse a head-on fight.
Everything Townes owns runs on power. Kill Cold Fusion Reactors and the Laser Turrets go dark, the lasers stop, and his base opens up.
His Point Defence Lasers shoot down rockets and missiles — bring shells, bullets and flame instead of a missile-only army.
Artillery out-ranges his defensive line. Siege him from outside the turret envelope rather than walking into it.
Alexander wins if the game goes long. Pressure her before the first Particle Cannon comes online — her opening is deliberately greedy.
Spread your base out. Clustered production is exactly what a Particle Cannon is priced for.
Kill the uplinks, not the army. Every destroyed Particle Cannon resets minutes of her plan.
Granger has no real tank line. A committed early ground push arrives before his second Airfield and he cannot answer it.
Mass anti-air rather than spreading it. Overlapping AA turns his aircraft from a threat into a donation.
His base defence is thin. Once you are inside it, you stay inside it.
Ta Hun Kwai has almost nothing that shoots upward. Aircraft are close to a free win if you get them out.
Rocket infantry in garrisons trade brutally well against his armour — a garrisoned building costs him tanks.
His tanks arrive veteran and early. Do not plan on winning the first ground engagement; plan on not taking it.
Flame, toxin and area damage delete his hordes. Dragon Tanks, Inferno Cannons, Toxin Tractors, napalm and carpet bombing all convert his army into nothing.
Never fight his infantry with your own infantry — his start veteran and there are more of them.
Artillery is the cleanest answer. He has to close the distance and artillery does not let him.
His tanks detonate when they die. Keep your army spread out or you will lose the fight you just won.
His nuclear reactors explode when destroyed — inside his own base. A single raid on his power does structural damage.
Engage at range. Every mechanic he has rewards you standing close to his units.
Bring detectors or you are not playing the game. USA: Sentry Drone. China: Listening Outpost, and Troop Crawlers in the army. GLA: Radar Van.
Assume any empty ground is occupied. Sweep suspected positions with area damage before you move through them.
Escort your vehicles. Kassad's Hijackers turn an unescorted tank into one of his tanks.
Go mechanised. Toxins do very little to vehicles and nothing at all to aircraft — an infantry army is a gift to Dr. Thrax.
Do not garrison buildings against him. Toxin Tractors clear a garrison faster than you can refill it.
Expect poisoned supply piles. Lingering toxin can stop your workers mining a pile you thought was safe.
Nearly everything Juhziz owns has to touch you. Kill it on the approach and it never functions.
Long-range units and aircraft are close to immune to his whole arsenal.
Sweep for Demolition Traps before expanding. He buries them on exactly the supply pile you were about to take.
You have no aircraft. Quad Cannons and Stinger Sites are not optional — build them before the enemy shows you why.
Your buildings leave holes. Rebuilding is cheap: fight like your base is expendable, because it partly is.
Your units cost more than theirs. Every engagement you take should be one you chose.
Do not lose parked aircraft. An Airfield raid costs you more than any ground trade will.
Keep five or more identical units together for the horde bonus — it is a free damage upgrade you are otherwise refusing.
Build a Listening Outpost early. It is the only cheap detection you have and stealth armies are common.
